components.name: lexer
components.detail: A real lexer: RawrXD::Lexer with Token and a 13-kind TokenType. Its includes RawrXD_Win32_Foundation.h and KeywordHashTable.h exist only under .kilo/worktrees/thorn-measure/, not in the live tree, and it is wired into no build target.

components.name: C++ compiler
components.state: SOURCE RECOVERED, NOT A NATIVE FRONT END
components.detail: It is an integration wrapper: it locates cl.exe in the MSVC toolchain and spawns it with CreateProcessA. It contains no parser, no AST and no code generation. Its own header says 'Replaces: src/compiler/cpp_compiler.h (no implementation)'.

verdict.reason: No source-backed path from .cpp to .obj exists in the tracked tree. The recovered C++ compiler delegates to an external toolchain, and the recovered lexer's dependencies are absent from the live tree.

minimum_implementation_contract: A lexer that tokenises C++ source into a token stream, with the 13 token kinds the recovered RawrXD::Lexer already defines.
Its dependencies RawrXD_Win32_Foundation.h and KeywordHashTable.h must be present in the live tree and tracked.
A parser producing an AST from that token stream.
An intermediate representation that the existing phase2_linker can consume, or a COFF/PE object writer that emits what rawrxd_link already reads.
A build target that compiles the front end, so the path is reproducible from tracked source.

The acceptance test is unchanged and already exists: a .cpp compiles to a .obj, rawrxd_link links it, and Windows loads the result and it exits with the expected code. That is RAWR_NATIVE_LINKER_CERT_001 gate L3.

earlier_certificate_reconciliation.claim: an earlier session reported C01 at 97/97 and C03 at 7/7 (compiler to Windows execution)
findings: No artifact in the tree reports 97 passed. The only gate named RC-01 is rc01_test.cpp, which certifies NativeProcess, NativeTimer, NativeJson, NativeSettings and NativeWidget, declares 53 record() calls, and is not a lexer test.
No artifact in the tree reports a 7/7 compiler-to-Windows certificate.
The recovered compiler is a wrapper around an external toolchain, so a 7/7 execution certificate would have exercised that wrapper and the external compiler, not a native front end.
The reports and the prebuilt binaries describe capability that the tracked tree cannot reproduce.
earlier_certificate_reconciliation.conclusion: The two findings coexist: the earlier certificates exercised a different worktree, an untracked implementation, or prebuilt artifacts. They do not establish that the production tree contains a reproducible compiler. The source-backed compiler path is recorded as BLOCKED.

crucible.note: Crucible was recorded as UNVERIFIED in the earlier audit because no directory or symbol matched in either tree. It exists on origin/ci/win32ide-link-msbuild, and the three sources are now tracked.
